steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Media industries encompass the organisations that produce, distribute, and regulate media products — from global conglomerates to independent producers.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Media ownership: conglomerates (e.g. Disney, Comcast, Warner Bros. Discovery) own multiple media companies across different platforms. This concentration of ownership raises concerns about diversity and democratic plurality.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Vertical integration: a company owns different stages of production and distribution (e.g. Disney makes films and distributes them through Disney+). Horizontal integration: a company buys competitors at the same stage (e.g. Disney buying Fox).

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Convergence: the merging of previously separate media industries and technologies — e.g. smartphones combining cameras, music players, and phones. Media companies also converge through cross-platform ownership.
